title: Add preserve_rowcount execution_option to momeize the rowcount in all cases
body:
### Describe the bug

Tring to migrate from psycopg2 to psycopg3 some queries.

Found that inserts do not return rowcount, even if the cursor correctly populates it.
Also while debugging this I've noticed that insertmanyvalues is not used in psycopg3, while is should (I think)

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.23 - any 2.0.x should be affected

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

psycopg2 2.9.9; psycopg 3.1.17

### Database Vendor and Major Version

postgresql - any

### Python Version

python 3.10

### Operating system

any

### To Reproduce

```python
import psycopg
import psycopg2
import sqlalchemy as sa

url = "postgresql://scott:tiger@localhost/test"


def using_driver(mod):
    if mod == "psycopg2":
        con = psycopg2.connect(url)
    else:
        con = psycopg.connect(url)
    with con:
        with con.cursor() as c:
            c.execute("create table tbl (col int)")
            c.execute("insert into tbl values (1), (2), (3)")
            print(mod, "insert values", c.rowcount)
            c.execute("insert into tbl select t from generate_series(%s::int,%s::int) as t", (5, 9))
            print(mod, "insert select params", c.rowcount)
            c.executemany("insert into tbl values (%s)", [(8,), (9,)])
            print(mod, "insert values exec many", c.rowcount)

        con.rollback()


print("driver")
using_driver("psycopg2")
using_driver("psycopg")


def using_sqlalchemy_conn(mod, echo):
    if mod == "psycopg2":
        url_driver = url.replace("postgresql", "postgresql+psycopg2")
    else:
        url_driver = url.replace("postgresql", "postgresql+psycopg")
    e = sa.create_engine(url_driver)
    e.connect().close()
    e.echo = echo
    t = sa.Table("tbl", sa.MetaData(), sa.Column("col", sa.Integer))
    with e.connect() as con:
        t.create(con)
        res = con.execute(t.insert().values([{"col": i} for i in range(1, 4)]))
        print(mod, "insert values", res.rowcount)
        res = con.execute(
            t.insert().from_select(
                ["col"],
                sa.func.generate_series(2, 7).table_valued("col").render_derived("t").select(),
            )
        )
        print(mod, "insert select", res.rowcount)
        res = con.execute(t.insert(), [{"col": 8}, {"col": 9}])
        print(mod, "insert values exec many", res.rowcount)

        con.rollback()


print("sqlalchemy conn")
using_sqlalchemy_conn("psycopg2", echo=False)
using_sqlalchemy_conn("psycopg", echo=False)
```


### Error

```
driver
psycopg2 insert values 3
psycopg2 insert select params 5
psycopg2 insert values exec many 2
psycopg insert values 3
psycopg insert select params 5
psycopg insert values exec many 2
sqlalchemy conn
psycopg2 insert values 3
psycopg2 insert select 6
psycopg2 insert values exec many 2
psycopg insert values -1
psycopg insert select -1
psycopg insert values exec many -1
``` 

The expected rowcount should be the same in psycopg and psycopg2

<details>
<summary> no longer relevant insertmanyvalue part </summary>

Also setting `echo=True` above shows the following log:
```

2024-02-06 14:52:07,020 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [no key 0.00016s] {'col_m0': 1, 'col_m1': 2, 'col_m2': 3}

psycopg insert values -1
2024-02-06 14:52:07,060 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine INSERT INTO tbl (col) SELECT t.col
FROM generate_series(%(generate_series_1)s::INTEGER, %(generate_series_2)s::INTEGER) AS t(col)
2024-02-06 14:52:07,060 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00018s] {'generate_series_1': 2, 'generate_series_2': 7}
```

the exec many uses insermanyvalues in psycopg2:
```
2024-02-06 14:52:07,020 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine INSERT INTO tbl (col) VALUES (%(col__0)s), (%(col__1)s)
2024-02-06 14:52:07,020 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00004s (insertmanyvalues) 1/1 (unordered)] {'col__0': 8, 'col__1': 9}
```
but not in psycopg3
```
2024-02-06 14:52:07,060 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine INSERT INTO tbl (col) VALUES (%(col)s::INTEGER)
2024-02-06 14:52:07,060 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00012s] [{'col': 8}, {'col': 9}]
```

this seems odd
